item.research_question: What is the microstructural stability of the AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr refractory metal high-entropy superalloy following long-duration thermal exposures at elevated temperatures?
item.processing_route: Arc melting of elemental metals (≥99.9% purity) under inert Ar atmosphere, inverted and re-melted five times, homogenised at 1400 °C for 24 h, furnace cooled to 750 °C at 10 °C/min then to room temperature; long duration thermal exposures of 1000 h at 1200, 1000, and 800 °C in Ta foil wrapped quartz tubes under vacuum, followed by quenching into ice water.
item.test_conditions: 1000 h exposures at 1200 °C, 1000 °C, and 800 °C; microstructural characterisation via SEM, EDX, and XRD.
key_findings: The initial nanoscale cuboidal B2 + bcc microstructure was found to be unstable following thermal exposures at all tested temperatures.
Extensive intragranular precipitation of a hexagonal Al-Zr-rich intermetallic occurred at 1200, 1000, and 800 °C.
At 1200 °C, the volume fraction of the Al-Zr intermetallic precipitates approached 50%.
At 1200 °C, the B2 phase was absent, indicating the material was in a two-phase field of bcc and hexagonal intermetallic.
At temperatures ≤1000 °C, the alloy existed in a three-phase field comprising bcc, B2, and hexagonal intermetallic phases.
The increased Zr content in AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr resulted in approximately double the volume fraction of Al-Zr intermetallic compared to AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr0.5 at 1200 °C.
Thermodynamic predictions using various databases showed significant deviations from experimental findings, particularly regarding the stability range of the B2 phase and Al-Zr intermetallics.
item.mechanism: The formation of the nanoscale B2 + bcc microstructure is driven by a miscibility gap between Zr and refractory metals; however, extensive precipitation of the Al-Zr intermetallic depletes the matrix of Al and Zr, stabilizing a bcc structure and preventing B2 formation at high temperatures. The B2 phase forms during cooling from a bcc precursor via spinodal decomposition plus ordering.
item.limitations: The authors state that thermodynamic databases currently do not offer high fidelity for predicting phase equilibria in these systems, and the B2 phase was not predicted by many databases or only at temperatures below 900 °C, contrary to experimental observations at 1000 °C.
item.future_work: Further experimental studies of phase equilibria are required to assess microstructural stability and provide data to refine thermodynamic databases for better predictive capability in RSA systems.
quotes: Crucially, the initial nanoscale cuboidal B2 + bcc microstructure was found to be unstable following the thermal exposures.
Extensive intragranular precipitation of a hexagonal Al-Zr-rich intermetallic occurred at all temperatures
Consequently, high Zr contents may be disadvantageous for RSA design as they favour the formation of the Al-Zr-rich intermetallic phase.
